Class DefaultRenderContext

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.toolkit.element.DefaultRenderContext
All Implemented Interfaces:
RenderContext
public final class DefaultRenderContext extends Object implements RenderContext
Default implementation of RenderContext with internal framework methods.

INTERNAL USE ONLY - This class is used internally by the toolkit framework. User code and element implementations should only interact with the RenderContext interface.

CODE SMELL WARNING: If you find yourself casting RenderContext to DefaultRenderContext in your code, this is a design problem. The only legitimate user of this class's internal methods is StyledElement.render(Frame, Rect, RenderContext).

Methods like withElement(Styleable, Style, Runnable), registerElement(Element, Rect), and stack manipulation are framework internals that should never be called directly from element implementations.

    • renderChild

      public void renderChild(Element child, Frame frame, Rect area)
      Description copied from interface: RenderContext
      Renders a child element within the given area.

      Container elements should use this method instead of calling child.render() directly. This allows the infrastructure to handle errors gracefully when fault-tolerant mode is enabled, and ensures that all rendered elements are properly registered with the event router, enabling them to receive key and mouse events.

      Example usage in a container element: 

      for (Element child : children) {
    context.renderChild(child, frame, childArea);
}
      Specified by:
      renderChild in interface RenderContext
      Parameters:
      child - the child element to render
      frame - the frame to render into
      area - the area allocated for the child

    • childStyle

      public Style childStyle(String childName, ChildPosition position, PseudoClassState state)
      Description copied from interface: RenderContext
      Resolves CSS style for a child element at a specific position with additional state.

      Combines positional pseudo-classes (:first-child, :last-child, :nth-child) with state pseudo-classes (:selected, :hover).

      Example usage: 

      for (int i = 0; i < rows.size(); i++) {
    ChildPosition pos = ChildPosition.of(i, rows.size());
    boolean isSelected = (i == selectedIndex);
    PseudoClassState state = isSelected ? PseudoClassState.ofSelected() : PseudoClassState.NONE;
    Style rowStyle = context.childStyle("row", pos, state);
}
      Specified by:
      childStyle in interface RenderContext
      Parameters:
      childName - the child name (e.g., "row", "cell")
      position - the position of the child within its siblings
      state - additional pseudo-class state (e.g., selected, hover)
      Returns:
      the resolved style, merged with the current context style

    • withElement

      public void withElement(Styleable element, Style style, Runnable action)
      Executes an action with an element and style pushed onto their stacks.

      The style is merged with the current style. Both the element and merged style are available via currentElement() and currentStyle(). This enables RenderContext.childStyle(String) to work without passing the parent.

      Internal use only - called by StyledElement.render().

      Parameters:
      element - the element being rendered
      style - the element's resolved style
      action - the action to execute

    • withElement

      public void withElement(Styleable element, Style style, CssStyleResolver resolver, Runnable action)
      Executes an action with an element, style, and CSS resolver pushed onto their stacks.

      The style is merged with the current style. The element, merged style, and resolver are available via currentElement(), currentStyle(), and currentResolver().

      Internal use only - called by StyledElement.render().

      Parameters:
      element - the element being rendered
      style - the element's resolved style
      resolver - the element's CSS resolver (may be null)
      action - the action to execute
